excerpt: The article states that less than 25% of meditation trials actively assess adverse effects, compared to 100% of pharmacology trials, and that spontaneous reporting may underestimate adverse-effect frequency by more than 20-fold. It concludes that assumptions of minimal adverse effects associated with meditation are largely based on a lack of research rather than substantive evidence.
overview: This is one of the strongest safety-related evidence items because it describes a measurement failure, not merely a list of possible harms. Without active adverse-event monitoring, low observed adverse-event rates cannot support claims of safety. The comparison with pharmacology trials highlights a reporting-standard gap.
title: Adverse Event Underassessment
